title: The menu and the record: unemployment and consumer prices in the United States (1946-1969) and Canada (1946-1969), yearly
source: Economic Report of the President, February 1971, Tables C-24 and C-45; Statistics Canada, Historical Statistics of Canada (11-516-X), second edition 1983, series D491 (Section D) and K8 (Section K)
series: us_unemp_pct: the unemployment rate of all workers in the United States, per cent (Table C-24, first column; 1948-1969, blank before 1948); us_cpi_1967_100: the consumer price index for city wage earners and clerical workers, all items, 1967 = 100 (Table C-45, first column); ca_unemp_pct: Canada's unemployment rate, annual average, per cent of the civilian labour force (D491, Canada total; it excludes the Yukon Territory, the Northwest Territories and Indians on reserves, and includes Newfoundland from 1950); ca_cpi_1971_100: the Consumer Price Index for Canada, total, 1971 = 100 (K8)

notes: The yearly inflation rates of the chapter's figure are the changes of the yearly average indexes (the book's calculation). The US columns are read from the text layer of the Economic Report of the President 1971 with pdftotext -layout: Table C-24 on PDF page 231 (printed page 225), the first figure of each year's line; Table C-45 on PDF page 255 (printed page 249), whose text layer reads the years 1968 and 1969 as '1958' and '1989' (rows e71_c45_1968 and e71_c45_1969 of phillips_facts): the script reads the lines after 1967 by their position. The Canadian rate before 1950 excludes Newfoundland (footnote 2 of D491: 'Includes Newfoundland beginning in 1950. First surveyed October 1949.'), so the figure starts in 1950.
